findings.title: Search position delta narrows to c_int before C abs
findings.analysis: In search_range, pos and oldpos have POSITION = less_off_t = c_long. After the pos == -1 branch, their difference is narrowed to c_int and passed to C abs. If the narrowed value is INT_MIN, C abs has no representable result and its behavior is undefined. Deltas beyond 32 bits also lose magnitude, so add_lnum may be skipped incorrectly. The condition is executed only when linenums != 0; file positions can exceed 32-bit range on the claimed x86_64 target. The oldpos/pos sentinel branch should be considered when replacing with full-width abs_diff.
findings.next_step: Root to disposition in maintained findings register, then fix with full-width difference after checking position/sentinel invariants and add a sparse >2 GiB regression where feasible.
findings.minimal_fix: In search.rs replace the narrowing/C abs with full-width `pos.abs_diff(oldpos) > 2048` after confirming both values are initialized valid POSITIONs; retain the existing -1 branch before this comparison.
findings.candidate_status: Full-width unsigned abs_diff replaces narrowed C abs; focused boundary regression pending independent execution.

findings.title: GNU regex syntax setting is mutated globally without restore
findings.analysis: compile_pattern2 calls re_set_syntax before each re_compile_pattern, discards the prior syntax returned by GNU regex, and has no restoration on success or on injected/native compile failure. re_set_syntax changes process-global native regex state; other callers could observe the changed syntax. SAFE-FFI-003 requires serialized/restored state or a documented scope proof. This record does not claim a concurrency exploit or a failed test.
findings.next_step: Root to disposition in maintained findings register; establish full callgraph/threading proof or scope/restore native syntax in M4.2, including error paths.
findings.minimal_fix: At minimum save `re_set_syntax` return and restore it after `re_compile_pattern` on both success/failure; process-global use still needs a serialized call scope or documented single-thread/no-concurrent-native-regex proof.
findings.candidate_status: Prior GNU syntax restored before success/error handling; focused regression pending. Serialized single-thread pager scope remains to be reviewed; no general library thread-safety claim.

findings.title: History temp file writes proceed when privacy mode change fails
findings.analysis: save_cmdhist derives a deterministic temp path by replacing the final byte of histname, then fopen(tempname, "w") creates or truncates it before make_file_private. make_file_private skips chmod when fstat fails or reports non-regular, and ignores fchmod(..., 0600) failure. Regardless, save_cmdhist writes history contents, closes, and renames the temp path over the history path without checking those results. A pre-existing permissive regular temp file retains its mode until chmod succeeds; failure leaves history data under those permissions. Even when chmod succeeds there is a create/truncate-before-chmod interval. A pre-existing symlink at the deterministic temp path is followed by fopen on Linux; the code still writes through the stream. The precise operational impact depends on path permissions and external actors.
findings.next_step: Root to disposition in maintained findings register and decide whether this is a legacy compatibility/security issue; test with a controlled existing permissive temp file and forced chmod/fstat failure, then handle creation mode, symlink and commit/error behavior in M3.4.
findings.minimal_fix: Create the temp file privately before any bytes are written (open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600 then fdopen), abort and unlink on mode/setup failure; check fclose/rename as commit operations. Preserve established overwrite behavior explicitly.
findings.candidate_status: Exclusive mode0600 same-directory temporary creation; check stream/close/rename, preserve previous destination and dirty state on error. Independent validation pending.

findings.title: Shell handoff can lose stdin when dup of fd 0 fails
findings.analysis: lsystem calls inp=dup(0) without checking -1, immediately closes fd 0 and may open the tty into fd 0. If the initial dup fails (for example descriptor exhaustion), both restoration attempts dup(inp) pass -1; the code closes fd 0 after system and continues with original stdin lost. The second restoration call return is unchecked even after successful initial duplication. This is a descriptor ownership/handoff failure; no reproducibility claim is made yet.
findings.next_step: Root to record/disposition, then fault-inject dup failure in an isolated helper session and require early abort or tracked restoration before closing fd 0.
findings.minimal_fix: Check the first dup(0) before closing fd 0; if it fails, abort helper handoff with original stdin/terminal state intact. Check restoration dup2 or equivalent and report failure before returning to pager.
findings.candidate_status: Acquire CLOEXEC stdin backup before teardown; checked dup2 swaps and restores; fatal cooked-state exit if restoration impossible. Independent validation pending.

findings.title: Logfile sync treats short or failed write as complete
findings.analysis: sync_logfile invokes write(logfile, buffer, datasize) but discards the ssize_t return, then sets wrote=true and breaks. A short successful write or -1 (EINTR/EIO/etc.) can leave the log block partially or wholly absent while the routine treats it as written. The broader M0-IO-002 finding covers src/output.rs::flush EIO, but this separate caller is not in its current evidence refs.
findings.minimal_fix: Loop over the remaining bytes on positive short writes, retry EINTR, and on permanent failure report/retain the incomplete log state rather than setting wrote=true.
findings.next_step: Root to decide whether to extend M0-IO-002 with this source path and regression or maintain this separate finding; no native-failure test has been run here.
findings.candidate_status: Retry exact remaining log bytes on partial/EINTR; permanent write/close failure disables log, diagnoses, and upgrades eventual success exit to1. End-log drain stops on failure. Independent validation pending.

findings.title: Position table scans use unsupported one-row geometry or new height before allocation growth
findings.classification: Independent ASAN reproduction: LESS_LINES=1 plus one-row PTY overflows get_scrpos_pos on empty and small startup inputs. Additional source hazards include pre-growth scans at new capacity and negative LESS_SHELL_LINES sentinel indexing.
findings.candidate_status: Minimum logical height two, shell-lines lower bound one; query/scan bounds use actual owned capacity including growth. Independent fixed-candidate validation pending.

findings.title: Permanent tcsetattr restoration failure is silent
findings.analysis: raw_mode(on) retries tcsetattr after EINTR but returns immediately on any other error. During raw_mode(false), the saved termios restoration can fail permanently; caller receives no status or diagnostic, and the code leaves in_raw_mode unchanged. The source comment says reporting permanent terminal errors is a tracked legacy gap, but the maintained findings register has no precise terminal-restore ID. The exact OS mode after failure is not re-read or proven.
findings.minimal_fix: Give the mode transition a checked result (or explicit recorded terminal-error state), preserve the prior saved mode until a verified successful tcsetattr, and report a permanent restore failure through the owning terminal/session cleanup path.
findings.next_step: Root to record/disposition; add an isolated PTY tcsetattr permanent-error fault oracle and verify primary error plus cleanup behavior without claiming mode restored.
findings.candidate_status: Record and diagnose permanent tcsetattr failure without claiming mode transition committed; upgrade successful quit status to1. Actual unsuccessful termios restore remains failure. Independent validation pending.
